requirements.evidence: All contract routes present with correct names/methods/middleware (routes/web.php:21-52: guest group, throttle:6,1 on password.email, signed+throttle on verification.verify, auth+verified on home). Login validates email:rfc,strict, throttles per lowercase email+IP with 5 tries, auth.failed/auth.throttle on email, session regenerate + redirectIntended(route('home')) (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:20-71). Register uses key str()->transliterate('register|'.ip), 5 attempts, error on email, Registered event, login, regenerate (Register.php:58-80). Password::defaults() configured once (AppServiceProvider.php:25). Reset rotates remember_token and fires PasswordReset (NewPasswordController.php:43-50). User implements MustVerifyEmail; resend skips verified users (EmailVerificationNotificationController.php:16-18). .env.example, phpunit.xml pins, ui.php in both locales. Gaps: requirement 9 says the rule applies to existing views too, but welcome/bulma-test are not touched and only a test guards it, so compliance there can't be confirmed from the diff; reset email is not lowercased while register stores lowercase.

conventions.evidence: Livewire uses #[Validate] + $this->validate() (Login.php:20-24, Register.php:23-27); controllers use inline $request->validate; named-route redirects everywhere; plain wire:model; Bulma markup with labels/aria; CHANGELOG and docs/business-rules.md updated; $fillable already set on User. Deviations: user creation is a write done directly in the component (Register.php:70-74) rather than an app/Actions class; Register mixes #[Validate] attributes with a rules() method for password (Register.php:38-43); forgot-password uses email:rfc while the others use email:rfc,strict (PasswordResetLinkController.php:28).

security.evidence: Rate limiting inside Livewire actions, Auth::check() guard against account switching (Login.php:36-40, Register.php:52-56), session regeneration on login/register, logout invalidates session + regenerateToken (LogoutController.php:16-19), signed+id/hash-checked verification via EmailVerificationRequest, forgot password always returns passwords.sent, remember_token rotation, {{ }} escaping throughout, no secrets in public props, password reset on failure. Minor: reset failure echoes __($status) which can be passwords.user, revealing whether an e-mail exists to anyone posting with any token (NewPasswordController.php:53-56); layout loads Bulma from a CDN without SRI as a fallback (components/layouts/auth.blade.php:13).

tests.evidence: Seven Pest files cover every requirement: pt_BR/en rendering (LoginTest.php:12-30), auth.failed and lockout messages, per-email lockout scope, remember token, authenticated-user unauthorized submit for both Livewire actions (LoginTest.php:145-157, RegisterTest.php:105-119), register throttle, confirmed rule, unique, password default, reset single email input, token tamper/wrong email, remember_token rotation, 429 throttles, verification id/hash tamper returning 403 and verifying nobody (EmailVerificationTest.php:47-68), resend for verified user, logout CSRF rotation and POST-only, config/env/phpunit pins, translation key parity, and a scan of all views for root-relative href/action (AuthConfigurationTest.php:50-59).

simplicity.evidence: Direct, lean controllers and components; one shared layout. Small unneeded pieces: an empty subclass of the framework EmailVerificationRequest (app/Http/Requests/Auth/EmailVerificationRequest.php:12-14) adds a file without behavior; CDN fallback branch in the layout; Auth::check() in submit duplicates the guest middleware (it does work as defense in depth).

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with PHPDoc, named constants MAX_ATTEMPTS/DECAY_SECONDS, consistent Bulma field markup, clear test names; no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. Small extras: audit-channel logging of failed/locked logins (Login.php:48,57) and a test for it, plus the CDN Bulma fallback in the layout, neither requested.

issues.explanation: The task says the route() rule also applies to the existing views, but they are not changed here, so compliance relies on them already being clean (only AuthConfigurationTest.php:50 checks it).
Returning __($status) on failure exposes passwords.user ('can't find a user'), which lets the reset endpoint confirm whether an e-mail is registered.
The user is created directly in the component instead of through an app/Actions class, which the conventions require for domain writes.
Register and login lowercase the e-mail but reset/forgot do not, so a user who types a different letter case gets a token/user error.
Uses email:rfc while every other e-mail field uses email:rfc,strict.
Mixes #[Validate] attributes with a rules() method; putting the password rule in the attribute style or all in rules() would read more consistently.
An empty subclass of the framework request adds a file without any behavior.
Adds an unrequested jsDelivr Bulma fallback with no SRI hash, which is an external dependency at runtime.
The registration lockout reuses auth.throttle, whose pt-BR text talks about login attempts.

review.summary: The change implements the full session-auth flow (Livewire login/register, logout, forgot/reset password, e-mail verification, pt_BR localization) against the contract, with sensible hardening and a thorough Pest suite that covers throttling, tamper, and unauthorized-call cases. The remaining problems are small: a possible e-mail enumeration through the reset error message, the user write not going through an Action, inconsistent e-mail normalization, and minor unrequested extras. I would approve it with nits.
